competitions.result: Third round — lost 3–0 to Luton Town in the second replay.
Runners-up — lost 2–1 to Arsenal at Wembley.
Winners — beat Everton 7–2 on aggregate in the delayed final of the 1985–86 competition.

overview: Liverpool finished second in the First Division, nine points behind Everton, in Kenny Dalglish’s second season as player-manager. Ian Rush scored 40 goals in all competitions, including 30 in the league. The domestic cup campaigns ended with a 2–1 League Cup final defeat by Arsenal and a third-round FA Cup exit against Luton Town after two replays.

There were two trophies: the Charity Shield was shared with Everton following a 1–1 draw, and Liverpool won the delayed Football League Super Cup final in September. They beat Everton 3–1 at Anfield and 4–1 at Goodison Park to win 7–2 on aggregate. Those final legs completed the competition begun in the previous season.

Barry Venison arrived from Sunderland and Sammy Lee left for Queens Park Rangers. John Aldridge joined from Oxford United in January, followed by Nigel Spackman from Chelsea in February. Earlier in the campaign, Liverpool had beaten Fulham 10–0 at Anfield in the League Cup second round.

Dalglish’s official profile describes this season as empty-handed. The fixture record, official Shield history and Guardian Super Cup account show a shared Shield and the delayed Super Cup win. The summary names those honours explicitly instead of repeating that description.

Rush’s physical departure to Juventus on 1 July 1987 is allocated to 1987–88. No claim about the earlier agreement or loan-back terms is made. The 40 goals include five in the Super Cup final and one in the Shield.
